results.summary_before: This design is a controller for a Pulsed Plasma Thruster (PPT) that generates a configurable number of pulses with adjustable frequency and pulse width, controllable via an I2C slave interface. It can also run with default settings using an override input, producing a pulse train at 0.25 Hz with 16 pulses. The design outputs pulse train status and a divided clock, and displays pulses on a 7-segment display. It is notable for being verified in simulation and prototyped on an FPGA, targeting space propulsion applications.

results.summary_before: This design is a basic sound synthesizer that generates a waveform and shapes it with an ADSR envelope. The waveform is selected between triangle and sawtooth, and the note frequency is chosen with four input bits while a separate clock sets the sampling rate. The envelope attack, decay, sustain and release stages are configured through the bidirectional pins, and the resulting sound is emitted on one output pin. Documentation is very thin, consisting only of a one-line description and a short test note, so the exact envelope resolution and output encoding are not specified.

results.summary_before: The design implements an asynchronous FIFO that buffers data between two clock domains with independent read and write clocks. It uses Gray-coded pointers and synchronization logic to prevent metastability, with full and empty flags indicating when the FIFO cannot accept or provide data. The documentation describes how to test by setting write and read enables and observing the flags and data outputs, but the pin list provided in the documentation does not match the actual pin names given in the project metadata. External hardware is minimal, likely just a way to drive the inputs and observe the outputs.
